open_questions: Depth varies 44.15% (sectors p_constant 0.004591, sector 68 8795 +/-904 ppm vs sector 92 13778 +/-1508 ppm) and transit depths chi2 21.279 p_consistent 2.395e-05 with 3 transits (share 0.4955); sector 92 amplitude 11078 ppm at p 0.738 d and sector 68 amplitude 9118 ppm at p 0.579 d near fast rotation expected for Teff 3484 — confirm depth is astrophysical with follow-up photometry and/or ground-based transit.
dossier.public_summary: A 2.5-hour, flat-bottomed 1.1% dip every 13.5 days repeats three times on a small 0.48-solar-radius M dwarf, giving a 5.5 Earth-radius signal with no significant secondary or odd-even difference and no nearby star able to mimic it. The star is spotted and variable, so the measured depth changes between sectors, but the duration, size and flat shape together are best explained by a planet pending more transits to test the depth scatter.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit (t14_h 2.998, b 0.1064) favors planet over V-shaped grazing EB, despite host variability.
Planet-sized (rp/rstar 0.1053) well below stellar limit; duration ratio 0.9372 and fit_log_density_ratio -0.09536 fit TIC star (rad 0.4827, mass 0.4807).
Phase-curve amplitude 968.2 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.08755 with chi2/dof 2.02 is low for close binary; favours planet.
No significant secondary (depth_ppm 1360, snr_at_half -0.916) and odd_even.diff_sigma 2.085 <4 with RUWE 1.642/flat shape argues against EB despite flags.
No Gaia star within 1 TESS pixel can cause dip; closest that could is 29.1 arcsec and centroid inconclusive not off-target, so off-target blend disfavoured.
